memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the regulations concerning animals, birds, every living thing that moves about in the water and every creature that moves along the ground. You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten." - Lev 11:46-47 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a summary and a calling: you must distinguish. Learn to tell the difference.

That word is worth sitting with. God did not simply want compliance from His people; He wanted discernment. He wanted them to become the kind of people who could look at the world and rightly tell what was of God and what was not.

Discernment is still one of the great needs of the Christian life — and it is in short supply. We live surrounded by voices, opinions, and teachings, many of them sounding spiritual, some of them wearing Christ's name while emptying it of meaning. John warns us plainly to test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out into the world (1 John 4:1). Hebrews says maturity belongs to those who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil (Heb 5:14).

Notice: trained by constant use. Discernment is not a gift that arrives one morning. It grows through steady time in Scripture, honest prayer, and life within a church that helps us see clearly.

And here is the good news for us: we do not stand before God hoping to be found clean. Christ has made us clean, once for all (Heb 10:14). From that secure place, we grow in wisdom — not anxious about our standing, but eager to know our God better.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How are you actively training yourself in discernment?
2. Which voices are shaping your thinking most at the moment?
3. What would help you grow in knowing God's Word more deeply this year?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ I am made clean once for all. Train my heart and mind through Your Word to tell the difference between what is true and what only sounds true. Amen.
